how_the_system_works.title: How the system works
how_the_system_works.intro: DriverLingo helps aspiring drivers prepare for the LTO non-professional and professional driver's license exams in English, Filipino, or Hiligaynon.

sections.heading: 1. Create an account
sections.body: Sign up with your name, email, and a password, or log in to an existing account. Your account keeps your exam history and progress saved across sessions.

sections.heading: 2. Choose your language
sections.body: Pick English, Filipino, or Hiligaynon at any time. Every question, answer choice, and explanation is available in all three languages so you can review in whichever one you understand best.

sections.heading: 3. Take a mock exam
sections.body: Answer timed practice questions drawn from the LTO reviewer question bank, covering road signs, traffic laws and regulations, and safe driving practices for non-professional and professional license categories.

sections.heading: 4. Review your results
sections.body: After submitting, see your score, your pass/fail status, and a full breakdown of every question with the correct answer and an explanation - so mistakes turn into something learned.

sections.heading: 5. Track your progress
sections.body: Every attempt is saved to your Exam History, so you can look back at previous scores and see how you're improving over time.

sections.heading: 6. Study offline
sections.body: Once you've opened the reviewer questions while online, they're cached on your device so you can keep practicing even without an internet connection.

sections.heading: Behind the scenes
sections.body: Administrators maintain and update the question bank and manage user accounts to keep the reviewer accurate and up to date.

privacy_policy.title: Privacy policy
privacy_policy.intro: We know studying for your license already means sharing enough paperwork with the government. Here's exactly what DriverLingo collects and why.

sections.heading: Information we collect
sections.body: When you register, we collect your name, email address, and a securely hashed password. As you use the app, we also store your chosen reviewer language and your mock exam attempts (answers, scores, and timestamps).

sections.heading: How we use it
sections.body: Your account details let you log in and keep your progress across devices. Your exam history lets you review past attempts and track improvement. We do not use your data for advertising, and we do not sell or share it with third parties.

sections.heading: Offline data
sections.body: Reviewer questions downloaded for offline use are cached locally on your device only, and are not shared with anyone else.

sections.heading: Data storage & security
sections.body: Your information is stored on our servers with hashed passwords and access limited to the development team maintaining the app. This app was built as an academic capstone project, so please avoid submitting sensitive personal information beyond what registration requires.

sections.heading: Your rights
sections.body: In line with the Philippine Data Privacy Act of 2012 (RA 10173), you may request access to, correction of, or deletion of your personal data at any time by reaching out through Contact Us.

sections.heading: Changes to this policy
sections.body: This policy may be updated as the app evolves. Continued use of DriverLingo after changes are posted means you accept the updated policy.

terms_and_conditions.title: Terms & conditions
terms_and_conditions.intro: By using DriverLingo, you agree to the following terms.

sections.heading: About this app
sections.body: DriverLingo is an independent study aid developed as a BSIT capstone project by students of West Visayas State University - Pototan Campus. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or connected to the Land Transportation Office (LTO).

sections.heading: Content accuracy
sections.body: We strive to keep questions, answers, and explanations accurate, but some entries are still undergoing verification against official LTO references. DriverLingo is meant to complement, not replace, official LTO reviewer materials - always confirm critical information with an authoritative source before your actual exam.

sections.heading: Your account
sections.body: You are responsible for the accuracy of the information you provide and for keeping your login credentials secure. Do not share your account with others.

sections.heading: Acceptable use
sections.body: Use DriverLingo only for personal exam preparation. Do not attempt to copy, resell, or redistribute the reviewer content, and do not misuse the app in a way that disrupts the service for other users.

sections.heading: Limitation of liability
sections.body: DriverLingo is provided as a study tool, "as is," with no guarantee of exam results. The development team is not liable for outcomes of your actual LTO exam or for decisions made based solely on this app's content.

sections.heading: Changes to these terms
sections.body: These terms may be updated as the app is improved. Continued use of the app after changes are posted means you accept the updated terms.

items.question: What is DriverLingo?
items.answer: DriverLingo (LTO Exam Reviewer Mobile App with Hiligaynon Translation) is a mock-exam reviewer that helps aspiring drivers prepare for the LTO written exam in English, Filipino, or Hiligaynon.

items.question: Is this an official LTO app?
items.answer: No. DriverLingo is an independent study aid built as a BSIT capstone project by students of West Visayas State University - Pototan Campus. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or connected to the Land Transportation Office.

items.question: Why Hiligaynon?
items.answer: Existing LTO reviewers are only available in English and Filipino, which leaves out Ilonggo/Hiligaynon speakers who are less comfortable in either language. DriverLingo translates every question, choice, and explanation into Hiligaynon so more drivers can prepare with confidence.

items.question: Does the app work offline?
items.answer: Yes. Once you have opened the reviewer questions at least once while online, they are cached on your device so you can keep studying without an internet connection.

items.question: Is DriverLingo free?
items.answer: Yes, DriverLingo is free to use.

items.question: How accurate are the questions and answers?
items.answer: Content is sourced from LTO reviewer materials, but some entries are still being verified against official references. If you notice an answer that looks incorrect, please let us know through Contact Us so it can be corrected.

items.question: Can I retake a mock exam?
items.answer: Yes, you can take as many mock exams as you like. Note that this is different from the real LTO exam, where failing three official attempts means a two-year wait before you can reapply.

items.question: Some Hiligaynon text still shows English or Filipino words - why?
items.answer: A few technical and legal terms used in traffic law do not have a direct Hiligaynon equivalent, so they are kept in their original language for clarity.

items.question: What devices does DriverLingo support?
items.answer: DriverLingo currently runs on Android phones and tablets.

items.question: How do I switch between light and dark mode?
items.answer: Go to Settings > Appearance and choose System default, Light, or Dark.
